messages.author: 39067cd82e77093b
messages.subject: Unexpected behavior of stat_contour
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to generate quantile contours for many curves.
As an example consider the profiles of the "sliced" volcano, ie i=1:87
slices volcano[i,1:61].
It is a little bit tricky because for any given x=1:61, several of the
slices may have the same height and
gstat_contour cannot deal with a multivalued "z" coordinate, ie, the
coordinate that identified the slice here.

Here is the code to do provide unique quantile values for every x and
height.

require(ggplot2)
Q <-apply(volcano,2,rank,ties.method='random')
profiles <-cbind(melt(volcano),(melt(Q)[,3]-.5)/87)
colnames(profiles) <-c("SliceNo.","x","height",'Q')
profiles.Q <-profiles[order(profiles[,2],profiles[,
3],profiles[,4],decreasing=TRUE),]
profiles.Q.shifted <-rbind(profiles.Q[-1,],profiles.Q[1,])
ToRemove <-matrix(c(FALSE,apply(profiles.Q[,
2:3]==profiles.Q.shifted[,2:3]
,1,all)
[1:nrow(profiles.Q)-1])
,ncol=1)
profiles.unique.Q <-data.frame(apply(profiles.Q[-which(ToRemove),2:4],
2,rev))

When I try to plot this, the resulting contours are not continuous as
they should be.

Graph<-ggplot(profiles.uniqueQ,aes(x=x,y=height,z=Q))+
stat_contour(linetype=1,size =
0.25,colour="grey50",breaks=seq(from=0.05,by=0.05,to=0.95))+
stat_contour(linetype=1,size =
1,breaks=seq(from=0.25,by=0.25,to=0.75))
print(Graph)

Any ideas?

messages.author: 4c2460918214ec91
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected behavior of stat_contour
parts:
Martin,

I gave it a decent look, but I have no idea. Assuming profiles.unique.Q  is all fine and proper, I would not expect this behavior either. I'm curious what the problem is. 

It might be worth generating a more simple example with synthetic data (where you dont have to filter for uniques) and seeing if you get the same problem.

James

parts:
Hi, let me start at the beginning:

The volcano data set has the heights specified as a 87 by 61 matrix at
a rectengular mesh of grid points: say 87 latitudes and 61 longitudes.

Objective:
Examine the height distributions at individual longitudes and pooling
over latitudes.
In my real world data set, longitude translates to time, latitude is a
sample-ID and height is a concentration.

Method:
For each longitude separately, rank the heights and divide the ranks
by the number of latitude values (87) to obtain approximate quantiles
q.
Plot contours of equal q in the (longitude, height)-plane using
geom_contour.

My code:
require(ggplot2)

Ranks <- apply(volcano,2,rank,ties.method='random')
# ie ranking is done for each value of the 2nd index (longitude)
separately.
q <- Ranks/87
profiles <- cbind(melt(volcano)[,2:3],melt(q)[,3])
colnames(profiles)<- c("longitude","height",'q')
profiles.df <- data.frame(profiles)
Graph<-ggplot(profiles.df,aes(x=longitude,y=height,z=q))+
stat_contour(linetype=1,size =
0.25,colour="grey50",breaks=seq(from=0.25,by=0.25,to=0.75))
print(Graph)

Problem:

Error in storage.mode(z) <- "double" :
(list) object cannot be coerced to type 'double'

What am I doing wrong here?

Martin

messages.author: 70ab9fabb9f066d8
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected behavior of stat_contour
parts:
So, I suspect it isn't working because contour is wanting a complete grid...?

Seems like you want lines joining quantiles of height within longitude
so how about:

probs <- seq(0.25, 0.75, 0.25)
quants <- ddply(profiles.df, "longitude", function(df){
data.frame(q = probs, height = quantile(df$height, probs = probs))})

qplot(longitude, height, data = quants, geom = "line", colour = factor(q))

Charlotte
